task: Implement Option B open-result summaries and local collection pinning in the shared compiler.
observation: During G2 open-result summary implementation, empty collection literals (`[]`) infer an open `vector` summary rather than nullopt. Early passes like `infer_handler_reply_types` and constructor checks initially raised premature type conflicts against concrete annotations before body specialization could occur; deferring conflict analysis to statement checking and program closure (`check_closed_body_types`) cleanly preserved both the new generic conformance suite and historical teaching diagnostics.
impact: All forward G0 conformance tests pass while maintaining 100% regression parity on Phase 20-24 suites and teaching diagnostic checks.

resolution.summary: Integrated open collection contextual specialization into constructor checking and handler reply inference, with program-closure unbound rejection emitting TYPE_AMBIGUOUS_OPEN_RESULT.

task: Implement generic nominal instance coexistence and exact specialization in the shared compiler.
observation: Decoupling nominal instance construction from the global template definition allowed multiple distinct generic instances (such as Box[value=int] and Box[value=string]) to coexist in the same program. Emitting generic Rust types with mechanical field names and enforcing single-monotype local bindings enabled 100% agreement between interpreter and native lowering without requiring source-level type argument syntax.
impact: All Phase 25 generic nominal tests, coexistence probes, and negative assignment mismatch gates pass across interpreter and native lowering.

resolution.summary: Constructed per-instance nominal types (Template[field=type]) during checking and lowered generic Rust structs (struct Box<F0>), while verifying single-monotype assignments with TYPE_MISMATCH.
